A [Product Requirements Document (PRD)](https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management/requirements) is a foundational guide written by a product manager to define what a product or feature should build, who it is for, and why it matters. It acts as a single source of truth to align engineering, design, and business teams before development begins.[[1]](https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management/requirements)[[2]](https://www.productboard.com/blog/product-requirements-document-guide/)[[3]](https://www.heretto.com/blog/product-requirements-document)

### Key Components of a PRD

- **Objective & Background:** The strategic reason for the project, problem statement, and expected customer value.
- **Target Audience & Use Cases:** User personas, target demographics, and real-world scenarios.
- **Functional Requirements:** Specific features, user stories, and system behaviors (what the product must do).
- **Non-Functional Requirements:** Performance, security, scalability, and usability standards.
- **Scope & Out-of-Scope Items:** Clear boundaries for what is included in the Minimum Viable Product (MVP) versus future phases.
- **Assumptions, Constraints & Dependencies:** Technical limits, regulatory requirements, or resource constraints.
- **Release Criteria & Success Metrics:** Quantifiable KPIs (e.g., conversion rate lift, reduced support tickets) that determine if the product is ready to launch.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Product_requirements_document)[[2]](https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management/requirements)[[3]](https://www.productboard.com/blog/product-requirements-document-guide/)[[4]](https://www.aha.io/roadmapping/guide/requirements-management/what-is-a-prd-(product-requirements-document))[[5]](https://www.jamasoftware.com/requirements-management-guide/writing-requirements/how-to-write-an-effective-product-requirements-document/)[[6]](https://carlinyuen.medium.com/writing-prds-and-product-requirements-2effdb9c6def)[[7]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y409ps_IyhU&t=11)[[8]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jdSFQG7dyrk&vl=en)[[9]](https://www.heretto.com/blog/product-requirements-document)

### PRD vs. Related Documents

- **BRD (Business Requirements Document):** Focuses on high-level business goals, revenue cases, and stakeholder buy-in.
- **MRD (Marketing Requirements Document):** Defines market opportunities, target markets, and customer demand.
- **Tech Spec (Product Specification):** Written by engineers to detail *how* the product will be built (architecture, APIs, and database schemas).[[1]](https://www.productplan.com/glossary/product-requirements-document)[[2]](https://www.chatprd.ai/learn/what-is-a-prd)

If you are writing one right now, tell me:

- **What kind of product or feature** are you building?
- **Who** is the primary user?

I can help draft a customized PRD outline or write specific user stories for you.
